content: 1. When completing and reviewing your page, ensure that you add a closing bracket ] at the end of the references section. 2. All team leaders must include a status update on their respective pages, detailing the total number of primary care topics and the number of completed ones. 3. Leaders are required to attend meetings to provide their updates. 4. Contributors must use the edit source option for their contributions; otherwise, they will be asked to stop contributing. 5. COVID-19 pages and reviewed primary care topics should be actively promoted on social media platforms. 6. Add all possible search terms for your topic under the synonyms and keywords section to enhance discoverability for readers. 7. For guidance on redirecting pages, refer to the provided instructions. 8. Aisha Adigun is responsible for regularly updating the COVID-19 pages. 9. Sara Haddadi will add additional references to the COVID-19 risk factors page as per Dr. Gibson's request. 10. The list of primary care topics should be updated continuously, including common complaints that bring patients to primary care physicians. 11. Before assigning a scholar to a topic, ensure the page is incomplete and not currently being worked on. 12. Contact other leaders to confirm whether a topic is included on their list. 13. Scholars working on primary care topics will receive additional credit for their CVs. 14. Sahar will expand the content on the algorithm page to make it more comprehensive and practical. 15. The cancer screening page should be redirected to the appropriate cancer-related pages. 16. Authors should conduct a literature review based on society guidelines (not family medicine guidelines) to find the most recent recommendations. 17. Pages should be developed and modified according to society guidelines rather than personal preferences. 18. Use the Resident Survival Guide template for structuring pages. 19. Algorithms can be created on paper or PowerPoint slides. 20. For example, refer to the Chest Pain Resident Survival Guide for guidance. 21. Leaders must create a list of the most common diseases related to their organ system and add it to their sandbox in an organ-based format. 22. Ensure every heading and subheading in COVID-19 pages has at least one reference. 23. Use the preferred template statements for the treatment section of medical therapy. 24. The dermatology list should be completed as soon as possible. 25. Farima Kahe, the oncology team leader, should create a landing page for common cancer screenings and redirect to relevant microchapters. 26. Focus on common symptoms like tinnitus, dizziness, fatigue, urinary retention, and nocturia, and include them in the primary care topics list based on the related organ system. 27. The English review process for COVID-19 pages is ongoing and should be completed. 28. Assign one or two scholars to each topic and guide them to write according to the provided template. 29. Avoid using a family-medicine-based approach as a reference; instead, use the society guidelines of the respective organ system for final algorithms. 30. Leaders must attend meetings to provide updates on their progress.
